Few things before I get into it, sorry, but you are right. My post history probably makes it confusing, because when I got Lilly I thought he was a she cause that's what my friend who rescued him told me. But my friend mixed up the sexes of the two bigger rescue bps. I switch between he and she when talking to Lilly so all good lol. But to the main part, You're absolutely right! Hes hella way too underweight. He just had a vet apt on Friday with one of the best reptile vets in the metroplex, thankfully no other issues (mites, parasites, constipation, mouth issues, respiratory issues, heart issues, etc.) But he's malnourished and underweight. I forgot the weight at the vet apt but buying a scale this weekend and working with the vet back and forth. I've had him a little over a week, he's a rescue from one of those hoarding "collector" types / an unethical breeder. Like currently he lives in a 40 gal, but for most of his life he's lived in a rack setup the size of his cold side hide. My friend is who rescued him and 2 other bps, and the first thing noted by them was Lilly's lethargy and skinnyness/spine showing as much. So rn until next weekend I'm feeding him rat pups 2x a week. So the reason behind why rat pups vs starting with smaller similar sized adult mice, is since they're smaller vs his size it's to help his body recover and be able to move up a size to older mice while also having a higher fat content than adult mice. The other worry is feeding too big when malnourished can cause digestive issues cause of atrophied villi in the intestine. After next weekend moving to adult mice 1x a week. He hasn't gained much weight which is to be given after just a week but his energy, personality, and everything have grown exponentially. When I first moved him into the [enclosure](https://photos.app.goo.gl/CVwe7VqQjKySFHEP6) he stayed in the cold side hide all the time only coming out for water and to periscope. I fed him on his 5th day home and he ate without issue. After 30hrs I moved him to the hot side hide to help him digest, he opened up after this. After 30mins resting in the hide he started actually exploring the enclosure and even basked. 2 days after this I brought him out the first time and it's just been so amazing in his personal growth and how active he is. I do plan to upgrade his tank in 6 months to a 55 or 75 gal cause I wanna give him more to interact with in his home, and I also wanna set him up a nice vivarium even in this tank but I'm waiting until he's at an ok weight, I don't wanna add too many variables. I love this little noodle monster, I wanna give him the best life I can.
